key_insight: POET-X scales the POET orthogonal-equivalence training idea to large language models by introducing memory- and compute-efficient ways to apply orthogonal transformations, preserving the spectrum of weight matrices while greatly reducing training overhead.
problem_solved: Reduces the high memory consumption and computational overhead of the original POET implementation so orthogonally reparameterized, spectrum-preserving training becomes practical for large-scale LLM training.
method: Retain POET's spectrum-preserving orthogonal-equivalence reparameterization but replace heavy matrix operations with scalable, low-memory parameterizations and algorithmic optimizations.

Factorize or structure the orthogonal transforms (e.g., block / low-rank / streaming-friendly forms) and integrate them into standard optimizer and dataloader pipelines to avoid extra full-matrix copies.
Profile and reduce runtime/memory bottlenecks so orthogonal updates can be applied at LLM training scale with minimal overhead while preserving stability benefits.
impact: Makes stable, spectrum-preserving orthogonal reparameterization feasible for training large language models, enabling better training stability and potentially larger effective batch/model sizes without prohibitive memory costs.

paper_title: POET-X: Memory-efficient LLM Training by Scaling Orthogonal Transformation
paper_authors: Zeju Qiu, Lixin Liu, Adrian Weller, Han Shi, Weiyang Liu
